findings.summary: prefix assertion is built from the verdict it renders
findings.text: follow-on: the expected prefix is built from verdict['estimated_tokens'], verdict['window_tokens'] and verdict['shortfall_tokens'] — the same verdict object the detail string is rendered from at reckon/crew/routing.py:3709-3716 — so the assertion pins the sentence's wording but cannot redden if those three figures are themselves wrong, which is the "existing total and window figures are asserted unchanged" half of the done-when; comparing them against the fixture's own window (passed to _backend_settings at tests/test_the_refusal_names_its_dominant_term.py:52) would make it independent.

findings.summary: surfaced CompetenceLimit message drops the new clause.
findings.text: follow-on: CompetenceLimit re-renders the context refusal from the verdict's scalars and drops verdict['detail'], so the message a dispatcher prints (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:1397, reckon/crew/dispatch_sessions.py:1744) never carries the new dominant-term clause; the clause reaches a coordinator only on the run record's competence.detail. node.py is outside this node's declared write scope, so the node recorded it as a follow-on rather than repairing it.
